rationale: B is more decision-useful because it better distinguishes why alternatives differ, ties forecasts to explicit mechanisms and reference classes, and gives clearer conditional guidance about when the recommendation would flip. It also includes implementation-risk and review checkpoints, which help a careful decision-maker act and monitor. A is solid and concise, but its numbers feel less grounded, and its recommended phased hybrid depends on a mid-project transition without much operational detail. B’s metrics are somewhat less directly aligned to “as quickly as possible” than A’s time-to-completion KPI, but overall it provides stronger comparative reasoning, uncertainty handling, and actionable follow-through.
